title: Mount Sharp rock analog database
notes: Rock analogs from Curiosity's traverse of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), Gale crater. Every number in 'samples' is a published APXS measurement copied unchanged from the PDS Geosciences Node MSL APXS supplements (drill tailings, drill fines and brushed rock), plus Curiosity CheMin mineralogy for Buckskin and ChemCam nickel for two iron meteorites found on Mount Sharp. Classes follow the Mount Sharp stratigraphy given in those tables. In-game boulders are analogs, not new measurements: each boulder takes one reference sample from its class and adds a small random variation within that sample's published analytical uncertainty (converted to 1-sigma with sigmaLevel, clamped at >= 0; values with no published uncertainty and upper limits are not varied; oxides, and metals when two or more are given, are rescaled to the sample's published total). Class physical/spectral properties marked in ext.proxyFrom come from a similar lithology and are not measured on that unit; null means unknown. FeO is total iron as FeO; oxides are wt%, traces ppm, metals wt%.

classes.name: Murray formation mudstone (lower Mount Sharp)
classes.summary: Finely laminated lake mudstone that makes up the lower slopes of Mount Sharp.
classes.formation: Mud settled in a long-lived lake in Gale crater; later groundwater added veins and concretions. Mount Sharp group, Murray formation (Pahrump Hills to Blunts Point members).
classes.whySample: Records a long-lived, habitable lake; drill targets preserve clay minerals and organic molecules.

classes.name: Vera Rubin ridge (hematite-bearing Murray)
classes.summary: Resistant ridge of Murray mudstone, seen from orbit as rich in hematite.
classes.formation: Upper Murray formation (Pettegrove Point and Jura members) hardened and stained by iron oxides from later groundwater.
classes.whySample: Shows how groundwater altered the lake beds after deposition; ties orbital hematite maps to rover chemistry.

classes.name: Glen Torridon clay-bearing unit (Carolyn Shoemaker fm.)
classes.summary: Clay-rich mudstone and sandstone of the trough south of Vera Rubin ridge.
classes.formation: Lake and river sediments of the Carolyn Shoemaker formation (Knockfarril Hill, Glasgow, Mercou, Pontours members), mapped from orbit as the strongest clay signal on Mount Sharp.
classes.whySample: Clay minerals form in water and preserve organics: a prime target for habitability studies.

classes.name: Mirador formation sulfate-bearing unit
classes.summary: Sulfate-rich layers higher on Mount Sharp, from the drying of Gale's lake.
classes.formation: Mirador formation (Dunnideer, Port Logan, Contigo, Catrimani members): sediments laid down as the climate dried, rich in magnesium and calcium sulfates.
classes.whySample: Captures the transition from a wet to a drier Mars recorded in Mount Sharp's layers.

classes.name: Amapari iron-rich bed (Mirador fm.)
classes.summary: Unusually iron-rich layer of the Mirador formation (about 40 wt% FeO by APXS).
classes.formation: A bed within the Amapari member of the Mirador formation with very high iron and low silica; its mineral origin is not described in this dataset.
classes.whySample: An anomalous composition worth sampling to understand iron enrichment in the sulfate unit.

classes.name: Stimson formation sandstone (Siccar Point group)
classes.summary: Cross-bedded sandstone from ancient dunes, lying on top of the eroded Murray mudstone.
classes.formation: Wind-blown basaltic sand that formed dunes after the lake beds were eroded, then hardened into sandstone (Siccar Point group, above an unconformity).
classes.whySample: Records a later, drier wind-dominated environment on Mount Sharp.

classes.name: Silica-rich alteration (Buckskin, Stimson halos)
classes.summary: Pale rock strongly enriched in silica by later fluids.
classes.formation: Silica added to (or other elements leached from) Murray mudstone at Marias Pass (Buckskin) and along fracture halos in the Stimson sandstone (Greenhorn, Lubango).
classes.whySample: Silica preserves textures and possible biosignatures; tridymite at Buckskin points to unusual volcanic input.

classes.name: Iron-nickel meteorite (found on Mount Sharp)
classes.summary: Dense, magnetic iron-nickel meteorite from a metal-rich asteroid, with a pitted, highly specular surface.
classes.formation: Metal from the core of a differentiated asteroid that fell onto Mars, where it was mechanically and chemically weathered.
classes.whySample: Its weathering on Mars records past water exposure and climate; rare exotic material for comparison.

samples.target: Buckskin drill sample, post-sieve (<150 um) dump pile
samples.site: Gale crater, Marias Pass, Murray formation (high-SiO2 laminated mudstone)
samples.prep: drill powder sieved to <150 um and dumped after CheMin delivery (rock interior; the same sieved fraction that CheMin analyzed)
samples.mineralsSource: CheMin XRD, column 'Bulk sample: XRD' of Morris et al. 2016 Table 2 (wt% of the whole sample, amorphous included)
samples.citation: Morris R.V. et al. (2016) PNAS 113(26), 7071-7076, doi:10.1073/pnas.1607098113, Table 1 ('Postsieve' column) and Table 2 ('Bulk sample: XRD' column). Sigmas and traces are from the PDS file msl_apxs_concentrations_mno_recalib.csv, row sol 1091 'Buckskin_post_sieve_dump_twk_corrected'.
samples.notes: VERIFICATION: I parsed Morris Tables 1 and 2 from the PMC HTML. All 13 oxides match the Postsieve column (Morris total 99.81), and all mineral values match Table 2, Bulk sample XRD (2-sigma: plagioclase 1.5, sanidine 0.9, magnetite 0.4, anhydrite 0.3, tridymite 1.0, cristobalite 0.4, amorphous 15). I downloaded the PDS MnO-recalibrated CSV and compared the row programmatically: every oxide, sigma and trace (Ni 132, Zn 326, Br 59) matches. The Morris text confirms the post-sieve dump on sol 1091 (the PDS start time is 1092M02:31:50, an overnight run). CHANGES: none. The PDS header calls the errors 'precision (repeatability)' and gives no sigma level. The MgO error (0.83) is larger than the MgO value. Trace sigmas: Ni 10, Zn 10, Br 5 ppm. Iron is FeOT in Morris. Do not use the PDS sol 1089 row 'Buckskin_post_sieve_dump_twk' (FeO 9.87, Cr2O3 0.20); Morris used the 'corrected' sol 1091 analysis. The APXS-constrained alternative gives tridymite 13.6 and amorphous 60 (a lower limit). PDS CheMin label cmb_491748904min10620482542ch00111p1 (verified): crystalline-only plagioclase 42.8, tridymite 34.1, sanidine 8.4, magnetite 6.9, cristobalite 6.0, anhydrite 1.8; opaline plus amorphous ~50 +/- 15 wt% of the total sample. Morris Table 1 also gives a calculated amorphous composition with SiO2 77.01.

ext.sigmaNote: 2-sigma (divide by 2 for 1-sigma). Level assigned at assembly: the mno_recalib header calls these errors 'precision (repeatability)' without a level, but the same row in the PDS4 APXS supplement ds01_3076.csv (urn:nasa:pds:msl_apxs_supplement_sols_0_3076) carries identical oxide errors and Ni/Zn/Br errors, and its supporting information (2021je007171r) defines every *_err as 'Statistical fitting error (two sigma)'. That supplement row lists Ni 133 and Zn 327 ppm (this record keeps the verified 132 and 326).

detectionFlags.MgO: value 0.82 <= stated uncertainty 0.83; treat as upper limit / near detection

samples.site: Gale crater, lower Mount Sharp, Murray formation (Sutton Island member)
samples.prep: natural (thin dust coat; Fe peaks reach steady intensity after ~2 shots; 9-point raster, 30 shots per point)
samples.mineralsSource: none (no XRD). The LIBS points are interpreted as kamacite; schreibersite is inferred at point #9 from coupled Ni and P enrichment (Meslin et al. 2017).
samples.citation: Meslin P.-Y. et al. (2019) 50th LPSC, abstract #3179, Table 1, row 'Aeolis Mons 001 (Egg Rock)', Ni (wt%) +/- 2-sigma, without point #9.
samples.notes: VERIFICATION: I downloaded the abstract and rendered Table 1 as an image. It shows sol 1505, Sutton Island, ~4 cm, 9 points x 30 shots, Ni/Fe peak ratio 0.214 +/- 0.026 and Ni 4.8 +/- 0.7 wt%, both without point #9. The header 'Ni (wt%) +/- 2-sigma' is visible in the image. CHANGES: none. Only Ni is quantified. Fe is not reported and is not computed here. Co (~0.5 wt% in typical irons) was not detected, and Ga, Ge, Ir and Au are below ChemCam detection, so no chemical group can be assigned. Meslin et al. 2017 LPSC #2258 (verified) gave an earlier estimate of ~8 wt% Ni from comparison with lab spectra; the 2019 calibrated value supersedes it. Meslin 2017 also describes the dust layer: residual dust peaks persist through the first 5 shots, and Fe peaks are steady after 2 shots. Wiens et al. 2017 MetSoc #6168 (verified) gives the size as 4 x 5 cm. Confidence is medium because this is a semi-quantitative LIBS value from a conference abstract. No APXS analysis exists.

ext.sigmaNote: Stated 2-sigma (statistical/counting precision); divide by 2 for 1-sigma. metalsSigmaWtPct is the 2-sigma Ni uncertainty from Meslin 2019 Table 1.

samples.site: Gale crater, lower Mount Sharp, Murray formation (Sutton Island member)
samples.prep: natural (dust-covered surface; 3-point raster, 30 shots per point)
samples.citation: Meslin P.-Y. et al. (2019) 50th LPSC, abstract #3179, Table 1, row 'Aeolis Mons 002 (Ames Knob)'.
samples.notes: VERIFICATION: I rendered Table 1 as an image. It shows sol 1577, Sutton Island, ~8 cm, 3 points x 30 shots, Ni/Fe peak ratio 0.384 +/- 0.017 and Ni 11.7 +/- 2.4 wt% (2-sigma). CHANGES: the prep now notes the dust cover, which Wiens 2017 describes ('the meteorite is covered in dust'). Wiens et al. 2017 MetSoc #6168 (verified) gives the size as 7.5 x 8 cm. It reports Ni/Fe peak ratios nearly identical to the ataxite Chinga (16.7 wt% Ni) and suggests a possible ataxite; the 2019 calibrated Ni is lower. Fe, Co and the other elements are not quantified. Confidence is medium because this is semi-quantitative LIBS from a conference abstract.

ext.sigmaNote: Stated 2-sigma (statistical/counting precision); divide by 2 for 1-sigma. metalsSigmaWtPct is the 2-sigma Ni uncertainty from Meslin 2019 Table 1.
